clue.text: Trash old sorted mail with two names

parts.note: to trash something is to bin it, throw it away

indicators.note: letters that are sorted are put into a new order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone throws away old post after sorting through the letters, each addressed with two names.
explanation.definitionFit: A binomial term, like a Latin species name, consists of two names: genus and species.

clue.text: Milk supplier runs into pig

indicators.note: runs goes into the word for pig, sitting inside it

parts.note: a pig of a person is a beast, someone brutish
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A dairy farmer's mishap: something gallops into a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A mammal's mammary gland produces milk, so a bosom is a supplier of it.

clue.text: Wife about to leave NE city to settle down

indicators.note: the wife and the about letters depart from the city's name

parts.note: Newcastle upon Tyne is the big city of north-east England
CA (circa) is Latin for about

explanation.surface: A wife is about to quit a north-eastern city in order to settle down elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes W and CA out of NEWCASTLE, a city in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuggle in or settle down comfortably is the same idea: get cosy and still.

clue.text: Do well following month on the hard stuff

indicators.note: the do-well word comes after the month-on pair

parts.note: taken as written
to shine is to excel, to do well

explanation.surface: Someone thriving a month into a spell of heavy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicitly distilled whisky is the archetypal hard liquor, so it is the hard stuff in slang.

clue.text: He weds eine Frau illegally, leaving her with this?

indicators.note: something done illegally is crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A bigamist marries a German woman unlawfully and then walks out on her with a farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: The German words in the fodder fit the German farewell; 'eine Frau' means a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The German phrase for goodbye is what you say when parting, leaving someone with a farewell.

clue.text: It helps you pick something to drink after close of business

indicators.note: the drink word comes after the close of business

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A suggestion of a drink once the working day is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin flip decides between options, so it helps you choose; also an even chance.

clue.text: Company climbing with dog come to pass

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A firm going up a hill with a dog, both coming along to pass by.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen or take place is to come to pass.

clue.text: Quiet popular bishop, one that supports member

parts.note: SH is a call for quiet
IN means fashionable, popular
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-liked, quiet bishop who backs one of his flock.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the bone bearing the lower leg, and a leg is a limb or member.

clue.text: Enable pi to be computed but not refined

indicators.note: letters to be computed are worked over, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rather coarse instruction to let a computer work out the value of pi.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebeian means common, vulgar, lacking refinement.

clue.text: Evergreens lose energy with their leaves prickling

indicators.note: the trees drop the energy letter

parts.note: pines are evergreen trees
E is the abbreviation for energy in physics
and means with, together
the leaves of pine trees are needles

explanation.surface: Fir trees running out of vigour, their foliage turning spiky.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the tingling, prickling feeling in a limb as circulation returns.

clue.text: Stand briefly by side of cricket pitch to relax

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, the last letter dropped

parts.note: an easel is an artist's stand
the off side is one half of a cricket field, the other being the leg or on side

explanation.surface: A painter sets up a stand beside a cricket ground to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the last letter from EASEL. In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is a phrasal verb for slackening or relaxing effort.

clue.text: List clubs cutting latest brand

indicators.note: the clubs letter cuts into the middle of the other words

parts.note: IN means in fashion, the latest thing
a brand of goods is a product line
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A shop's inventory, with golf clubs breaking into the newest brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' is a verb here: a ship that lists leans to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A listing ship leans or tilts, and to lean is to slope or tilt.

clue.text: In which small beers are discounted?

definitions.text: In which small beers are discounted?

parts.note: ales are beers

explanation.surface: A wry question about where little drinks go cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: S plus ALES, and an event at which goods, beers included, are discounted.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops hold bargain events where prices are discounted, and plural reductions events are these.

clue.text: You are wearing cool fur that could be covered

parts.note: IN means trendy, cool

indicators.note: the fur is worn by the you-are letters, which go inside it

parts.note: sable is a luxurious fur
UR is text-speak for you are

explanation.surface: Wearing a fashionable fur coat that could be insured.
explanation.definitionFit: Something an insurer will accept as a risk can be covered by a policy.

clue.text: Undisclosed reason Dad had engine fixed?

indicators.note: an engine that is fixed has been worked on and reassembled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Father had the car engine repaired, perhaps with some secret motive.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret motive or concealed plan behind someone's actions is an undisclosed reason.

clue.text: German governor regularly duelled during spat

indicators.note: the picked letters sit during, inside, the spat

parts.note: a spat is a short gaiter worn over the shoe

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: German officials fought duels regularly in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spat' looks like a quarrel; it is a cloth covering for the ankle, a gaiter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gauleiter was the Nazi party's regional governor of a district.

clue.text: People play this in Israeli flat? On the contrary

parts.note: an Israeli is loosely taken as a Jewish person
the contrary of flat in music is sharp

explanation.surface: A musical instrument heard in an apartment in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: A jew's harp is a small instrument held against the teeth and twanged; 'On the contrary' swaps flat for its musical opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A jew's harp is a small musical instrument, so it is something people play.

clue.text: Big weapon old doctor stored in a vault

indicators.note: the old doctor letters are put away inside the a-vault letters

parts.note: a vault is a burial chamber, a tomb
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: An elderly physician keeps a huge weapon hidden in a vault.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear fission bomb is a massive weapon.

clue.text: English theatres respecting north regret backing impresario

parts.note: NT is the National Theatre and REP a repertory theatre, two theatres
RE means regarding, respecting

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the regret word is read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: An English impresario's regrets over theatres in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario is a business promoter of shows, one kind of enterprising business person.

clue.text: Drive and look around in the same place

indicators.note: the look letters go around the same-place letters

parts.note: LO is an old word meaning look
IBID, short for Latin ibidem, means in the same place in references

explanation.surface: A motorist going for a drive and looking round the same spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual drive or desire.

clue.text: Emphasise English MPs should avoid sewer

indicators.note: the letters for English and MPs keep away from, leave, the sewer word

parts.note: a sewer here is someone who sews, a seamstress
AMs are Assembly Members, the Welsh counterpart of MPs

explanation.surface: Stressing that English politicians ought to keep clear of the drains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' is not the drain but one who sews. AMs were members of the Welsh Assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to emphasise it.

clue.text: Small music company (British) always returns note

parts.note: EMI is a famous record company

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the always word is read backwards

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A small British record label keeps bringing back a single note.
explanation.definitionFit: A semibreve is the musical whole note, worth four crotchets.

clue.text: Narcotic leaf insect picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for insect is taken by its sound

parts.note: a beetle is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug found on a drug plant's leaf is lifted off.
explanation.definitionFit: Betel leaf is chewed with areca nut across South Asia as a mild stimulant.

clue.text: Throw out six in European court

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Six people are ejected from a European court.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel a tenant, to throw them out.

clue.text: Advocate job in drink

indicators.note: the job goes in the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A barrister working at a pub or bar job.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a passionate supporter of a cause, an advocate.

clue.text: After training, I learnt where to go in the army

definitions.text: where to go in the army

indicators.note: letters in training are drilled into a new shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recruit after basic training reports what was learnt about army life.
explanation.definitionFit: A latrine is a military toilet, and where to go is a euphemism for the lavatory.

clue.text: Footballer collects books, one of many on beach

indicators.note: the footballer collects, takes inside, the books

parts.note: Pele was the great Brazilian footballer
B is book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: A footballer gathers books on a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Small rounded stones cover shingle beaches in their thousands.

clue.text: FT female quits, enraged, attracting huge interest

parts.note: the clue appears in the Financial Times, so FT is us, the paper speaking

indicators.note: the female letter quits, leaves, the enraged word

parts.note: furious means enraged

explanation.surface: A woman resigns from the Financial Times in a rage, causing a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' is the lending sense: a usurious loan charges a crippling rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Usury is charging exorbitant interest, so a usurious loan attracts a huge rate.
